newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan troops take town in eastern Zaire -paper.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan troops take town in eastern Zaire -paper.

text.p: Ugandan troops crossed into eastern Zaire on Thursday to attack Ugandan rebel bases and seized a town in the area, the government newspaper New Vision reported on Saturday.
The daily said 23 rebels were killed during the attack on Thursday, when the Ugandan army seized the town of Kasindi and the Virunga hills, which are 10 km (six miles) inside Zaire.
"We are fed up with these bandits. We are going to finish them," Lieutenant-Colonel Geoffrey Muheesi was quoted as saying. He added that his soldiers would not be leaving the area.
He accused Zaire of equipping the rebels, who have been raiding western Uganda. The Zairean government has denied this.
Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni went to the southwestern Ugandan border area on November 21 and pledged to pursue "dissidents and invaders" back to their bases in Zaire.
During that visit to Kasese he accused "Sudanese financiers" of being behind the rebel attacks, but absolved Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko of responsibility.
